summary: Verified the api.ts + net-diagnostics + NetworkContext refactor. Backend regression 9/9 green (health, register, duplicate-email 400 with 'email already registered', login, wrong-password 401 with 'Incorrect email or password', /auth/me, PUT /api/users/me persistence, demo@demo.com login). Web UI: signup lands in onboarding; login with demo@demo.com/Demo1234! lands on /connect; wrong password shows exactly 'Wrong email or password. Please try again.' with NO 'Try again' retry link; duplicate email shows 'This email is already registered. Try logging in instead.' with no retry link; connect/moments/voice/chats/notifications/profile all render authenticated with no offline banner; /dev-diagnostics renders (testID dev-diagnostics-screen) with all required rows (Base URL, Host, Source, Scheme, Platform, Device internet, Health /api/health = OK (200), Latency, Session token = present), 'Run again' (diag-rerun) re-probes successfully, and NO JWT/token value is leaked. Onboarding progressed through the first 3+ in-page steps without any error or offline banner (test script could not auto-complete every picker step but no regression observed). No hardcoded backend URL detected in api.ts; getApiUrl uses window.location.origin on web as designed.
critical_code_review_comments: api.ts:29-48 correctly excludes localhost/10.0.2.2/0.0.0.0 on native and falls back to an empty string; no hardcoded preview URL remains — matches the RCA.

dev-diagnostics.tsx:38-43 exposes only the *source* of the base URL ('EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL', 'expoConfig.extra.backendUrl', 'window.location.origin', or 'none'); getAuthToken() is rendered only as 'present'/'none' — verified no token value leaks.
NetworkContext probe correctly hits /api/health (line 61) instead of /api/auth/me; failureRun threshold of 3 avoids false-positive offline banner.

auth.tsx humanizeError regexes match backend detail strings exactly (verified in backend test): /incorrect email or password/i and /email already registered/i. Retryable is only set when e is ApiError && e.kind !== 'http', so wrong-password (HTTP 401) never shows the 'Try again' link — verified in UI.
